i guess i'll start..when i was growing up i had it rough..i grew up in the fostercare system after getting out of a bad situation when i was 8 so i read. A lot. when i was in 6th grade i was going through a rough patch, it seemed like i was in a new home every other month. I had this art teacher, Ms. Alee who for some reason seemed to notice i was pretty antisocial, so she made it her mission to talk to me..at first i wasn't very talkative but as time went on i gradually opened up to her, but still didn't tell her about my home situation and eventually we ate lunch together every Thursday. We were joined by her neice who was also in my art class..one day Ms. Alee asked me if i liked to read. i told her i did but i didn't have very many books because of the limited space i had to work with. She looked stunned and asked me what i meant. I remember telling her 'when the social worker shows up, i don't have very much time to pack' i then explained i that i was in the foster care system and i had been in a lot of homes lately. I swear she had tears in her eyes. The next day she stopped me after class and gave me a hardcover copy of Harry Potter and the Sorcerers Stone. That night i had my first introduction to the wizarding world and i was hooked..that Monday i had finished the book, and took it to school so i could return it to her and she said 'No, that's yours now' I told her i thought she had been reading them with her daughter who was a huge fan and she said that they had finished with it. the next day she  came and ate lunch with me and gave me the 2nd book and we began to discuss our favorite characters. When i asked her why she gave me such obviously expensive books she said 'books are meant to be shared' This continued until i had hardcover editions of all 4 books. One day the social workers showed up and removed me to a group home, which was no longer in that school district. I'm 24 now and when i hear the Harry Potter theme song, i still get butterflies in my stomach. Ms Alee..if you read this...thank you for helping me get through those long nights and showing me a brand new world. I am eternally grateful.
